sample_unit: simulated interruption conversation transcripts (30 per condition in reported cells)
models_evaluated: Llama (one of four deployment-oriented non-reasoning LLM configurations; other three not named in text)

links.outcome: Preservation of clinically required content after simulated patient interruptions in voice-agent transcripts
links.effect: Competitive FAQ interruption produced 30/30 provision-coverage failures for all four models (Wilson 95% CI 88.6-100.0%); baseline 0/30 for three models, 4/30 for Llama.
links.quote: Rankings differ across cells, and competitive FAQ interruption produced 30/30 provision-coverage failures for all four models (Wilson 95% CI: 88.6-100.0%; baseline 0/30 for three, 4/30 for Llama).

unlisted_practices: Testing conversational voice agents for recovery of clinically required content after patient interruptions, reported per cell
Using an apology marker ("sorry to interrupt") to shift interruption recovery

screen.reason: The study develops and applies a benchmark evaluation to test the safety and robustness of clinical conversational voice AI under patient interruptions across clinical history-taking and FAQ tasks.
